headword: Besant, Bezant, Bessant, Beasant, Bes[z]ant?, Beaza[nt]?, Bayzand
meaning: of Byzantium (?), i.e. an immigrant from Byzantium; or possibly from the coin, the bezant
author_comment: 'To oone he gave fyve [...] or besauntis,' 1382, Wyclif [...] xxv. 15); v. H.E.D. for va[rious] instances. 'A bisaunt, bezant, [...] bizantine was an old coin both in gold and silver, and so called from having been minted at Byzantium. The silver bezant passed current for 2s. or thereabouts' (Pipe Rolls, vol. iii. p. 74: Pipe Roll Soc.). As almost every other coin has its representative in our nomenclature so may this. More probably, however, like Turk and Saracen, it is local, denoting an immigrant from Byzantium. [Headword and etymology printed on p. 97, where part of the headword and commentary is covered by a folded flap of paper in the scan.]
